view: This print turns on three lines: the Q4 revenue guide against a consensus that looks conservative, the gross-margin and EBITDA guide, and what Beck says about a new Neutron date. The company has a record of sandbagging. Q2 revenue was $234m against a $225-240m guide, non-GAAP gross margin was 41.5% against guide, and adjusted EBITDA was -$8.8m against a guide of -$20m to -$26m. The Q3 guide midpoint was a large raise. So a Q3 beat at or above the top of the guide is likely and expected. The Q4 consensus of about $267m (+4% q/q) sits below the recent +10-17% sequential trend, and Q4 is seasonally strong for Space Systems deliveries. I lean toward a Q4 guide above consensus. That is the case for upside. But the two most recent setups argue against reading too much into it. In May a revenue-guide raise produced +34%, with Neutron 'on track' and a hot tape. In August a revenue-guide raise produced a flat reaction, because the GAAP gross-margin guide of 29-31% came in well below the Street's roughly 37.6%. This time the margin guide is unknowable from outside. Neutron has slipped for the fourth time, with no date. Beck said a precise date will follow demonstrated progress (tank qualification extends into early 2027), so the call is more likely to give 'H1/mid 2027' or nothing than a firm date. Q4 Electron cadence looks thin: 2 launches from 10-01 to 11-09 (10-23 and 11-02), against 6 in Q3. The stock also rallied about 10% today with a high-beta tape, which takes some of the washed-out-positioning cushion off the table. Overnight index moves of ±3% have been normal this week, and this stock has a beta near 3. Net: a mild lean up from the guide pattern and washed-out sentiment, nowhere near a bettable edge.
unpriced: Possibly the Q4 revenue guide. Consensus of about $267m implies +4% q/q while the company has guided +10% or more sequentially for three straight quarters and beat its own EBITDA guide by a wide margin. That consensus figure is undated, so I cannot prove it is stale, and the market knows the company sandbags. The Neutron news is not unpriced: it is a dated 8-K followed by a roughly 21% fall and target cuts.

recommendation.reason: The guide-beat pattern and a Q4 consensus that looks low point mildly up. But the last guide beat (August) went flat on a margin guide nobody can see in advance. Neutron has no date, and today's 10% beta rally plus a fragile tape leaves the overnight open dominated by things outside the release. No mechanism here reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide midpoint at or above about $285m, with non-GAAP gross margin guided back near 40% and a specific H1 2027 Neutron launch window, would make up the clear call. A margin guide at or below Q3's 35-37% non-GAAP, or Neutron opex raised with no date, would make it down.

self_critique: The case for long is stronger than 56 suggests. The stock is down 61% from its high and the bad news is fully out. The company systematically beats its own guide, and the Q4 consensus looks too low. In May the same mix of a beat, a raise and a backlog headline produced +34%. Backlog will likely jump to around $3bn+, and an EBITDA beat is likely. A clean beat-and-raise into a washed-out holder base could gap the stock 10%+. The case for short is a repeat of August: a margin guide that disappoints, plus Neutron R&D spending that runs longer and pushes EBITDA profitability out by quarters, after a ~20% two-day bounce in a fragile growth tape, with puts bid. Neither side has evidence I can verify from outside on the margin line, which is the line August turned on.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line the stock trades on, read the last reactions) did the most work: the May/August pair showed that the margin guide, not revenue, decides between a pop and a flat print. P4 helped me take Neutron off the table by showing the price fall and target cuts tied to it. The playbook has no step for a name whose overnight move is dominated by market beta (the prior 3 sessions were -12/+15/+10 on no company news); a line on separating beta from the print would help.
